Rashi on Pesachim 64a:10:1.hebrew: מפי חבורה - כולם הודו בדבר זה, לאוקומי מתני' דמשמע דבעי למעקר שם פסח מיניה, כגון שהיו בעליו טמאין בארבעה עשר, דסתמיה לשם פסח שני קאי, מש"ה בעי עקירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:10:1.english: From the mouth of the group - All of them agreed on this matter: to establish [our] Mishnah, which implies that one must uproot the designation of a Paschal offering from it, [as referring to a case] such as where its owners were ritually impure on the fourteenth [of Nisan], for without specification it stands for the sake of the second Passover; therefore, it requires uprooting.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:11:1.hebrew: הפסח נשחט בשלש כיתות - פסחי צבור, בין שהצבור מועטין ויכולין לישחט כולן בבת אחת, מצוה ליחלק לשלש כיתות זו אחר זו:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:11:1.english: The Paschal lamb is slaughtered in three groups - [With regard to] the Paschal offerings of the congregation, even when the congregation is small and they can all be slaughtered at once, it is a mitzvah to divide into three groups, one after another.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:1.english: Bowls of gold and bowls of silver - Large ladles to receive the blood in them.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:2.hebrew: שכולה כסף כו' - בגמ' מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:2.english: That is entirely silver, etc. - In the Gemara, [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:3.hebrew: ולא היו לבזיכין שוליים - רחבין מלמטה, אלא חדין תחתיהם, כדי שלא יוכלו לישב על הקרקע:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:3.english: And the bowls did not have bases - [That is,] wide at the bottom; rather, [they were] pointed underneath, so that they could not sit on the ground.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:4.hebrew: שמא יניחום - כהנים על גבי קרקע עד שיקבלו דם אחר, מחמת שהן מרובין, וישכחום, ויקרוש הדם ולא יהא ראוי לזרוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:12:4.english: Lest they set them down - [That] the priests [would set them] on the ground until they receive other blood, because they are numerous, and they would forget them, and the blood would congeal and would not be fit to sprinkle.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:1.hebrew: שחט ישראל - אם ירצה, שהשחיטה כשירה בזרים בכל הקרבנות:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:1.english: An Israelite would slaughter - If he wishes, for slaughter is valid [when performed] by non-priests for all offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:2.english: And a priest received - the blood in a bowl from the neck of the lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:3.english: He gives it to his fellow - For they stand in a row up to the altar.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:4.hebrew: מקבל את המלא - מיד הנותנו לו, ומחזיר את הריקן שחזר אליו מיד כהן הזורק:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:4.english: Receives the full [bowl] - From the hand of the one giving it to him, and returns the empty [bowl] that came back to him from the hand of the priest who sprinkles [the blood].

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:5.hebrew: זריקה אחת - בבזך עצמו זורק, ולא מתנה באצבע, שאין לך קרבן טעון אצבע אלא חטאת לבדה, כדכתיב "באצבעו":
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:5.english: A single sprinkling - He sprinkles [it] with the bowl itself, and not [as] an application with the finger, for there is no offering that requires [the] finger except a sin-offering alone, as it is written, "with his finger."

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:6.hebrew: כנגד היסוד - ברוחות שבמזבח שהיה יסוד תחתיהן, וזורק לזקיפתו של מזבח והוא נופל ליסוד. ולפי שאין היסוד מקיף את המזבח אלא את הצפון ואת המערב, כדתנן במסכת מדות (פ"ג משנה א), לכך הוצרך לומר כנגד היסוד:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:13:6.english: Against the base - On the sides of the altar that had a base beneath them; and he throws [the blood] against the upright wall of the altar, and it falls onto the base. And since the base does not surround the [entire] altar, but only the north and the west [sides], as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Middot (3:1), therefore it needed to state "against the base."

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:1.english: So [was] the procedure of the second and third [groups] - All as we have said.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:2.english: They recited the Hallel - [This] refers to all the groups.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:3.hebrew: אם גמרו שנו - כשהיו מתחילין לשחוט, מתחילין לקרות. ואם רבו הפסחים ומשך זמן שחיטתן עד שגמרו, ועדיין רבים שוחטין — חוזרין וקורין שניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:3.english: If they finished, they repeated [it] - When they would begin to slaughter, they would begin to recite [Hallel]. And if the Paschal offerings were numerous and the time of their slaughtering extended until they finished, while many were still slaughtering, they would go back and recite [it] a second time.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:4.hebrew: ואם שנו - ועדיין לא גמרה שחיטת פסחי אותה כת, שילשו, וכן השניה וכן השלישית. ואע"פ שלא אירע מעולם ששילשו, לפי שהיו שם כהנים מרובין ומהירין במלאכתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:4.english: And if they repeated [it] - And [if] the slaughtering of the Paschal lambs of that group had not yet finished, they recited [it] a third time, and likewise the second [group], and likewise the third [group]. And even though it never happened that they recited [it] a third time, [this was] because there were many priests there and [they were] quick in their work.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:14:5.english: They did not reach “I love [that the Lord hears]” - Even [the] first time.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:15:1.hebrew: אלא שהכהנים מדיחין העזרה - שאמת המים מהלכת בעזרה, וכשהן רוצין להדיח העזרה, פוקקין את נקב יציאתה, והמים פושטין והולכין על גדותיה ומדיחין את כל העזרה — שרצפה של שיש היתה כולה — ואחר כך פותחין הנקב והמים יוצאים. ובערב הפסח, מתוך שהדמים מרובים, היו מדיחין אותה; והכהנים היו מדיחין אותה בשבת שלא ברצון חכמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:15:1.english: Only that the priests would rinse the Temple courtyard - For a water channel runs through the Temple courtyard, and when they wish to rinse the courtyard, they plug its outlet hole, and the water spreads and overflows its banks and rinses the entire courtyard — for its floor was entirely of marble — and afterward they open the hole and the water flows out. And on the eve of Passover, because the blood [of the offerings] was abundant, they would rinse it; and the priests would rinse it on Shabbat, contrary to the wishes of the Sages.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:15:2.hebrew: מדם התערובות - המוטל על הרצפה, וטעמא מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:15:2.english: From the blood of the mixture - Which is lying on the floor, and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:1.hebrew: אונקליות - מסמרים שראשיהן כפופין למעלה, קרוק"ש (ווים, אנקולים) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:1.english: Unkelayot - Nails whose heads are bent upward; crocs (hooks, clasps) in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:2.hebrew: בעמודין - אלו עמודין קטנים הרבה וקרויין ננסין, כדאמרינן במס' תמיד (פ"ג משנה ה') דתנן: בית המטבחיים היה לצפונו של מזבח, ועליו שמונה עמודין וקרויין ננסין, וקורות של ארז על גביהן, ואונקליות של ברזל היו קבועין בהן, ושלשה סדרים שבהן תולין ומפשיטין:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:2.english: Into the pillars - These are very small pillars, and they are called nanasin [dwarfs], as we say in Tractate Tamid (3:5), where we learned in a Mishnah: "The slaughterhouse was to the north of the altar, and upon it were eight pillars, and they are called nanasin, and cedar beams [were] on top of them, and iron hooks were secured into them, and [there were] three rows [of hooks] upon which they would suspend and flay [the offerings]."

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:3.english: Secured - In the [Temple] courtyard, in the place of the slaughterhouse.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:16:4.english: Smooth - Smoothed, [with] their bark peeled off.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:1:1.hebrew: קשיא מליקה אמליקה - דס"ד בארבעה עשר קאמר, וקתני דעבר אמליקה דומיא דשאר קרבנות, ועוד דקא חשיב ליה כשחיטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:1:1.english: Pinching contradicts pinching - For [we] initially thought [the baraita] is speaking of the fourteenth [of Nisan], and it teaches that one transgresses for pinching, similar to other sacrifices, and furthermore that it considers it like slaughtering.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג ולטעמיך תיקשי לך היא גופא דקתני רישא לא אמרו אלא פסח בלבד - אבל אשאר קרבנות לא מחייב, והדר תני אחד המולק ואחד המזה:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:2:1.english: Thus we read: And according to your reasoning, ask about [the baraita] itself, as it teaches in the first clause, "They said [that this applies] only to the Paschal lamb" - but for other offerings one is not liable; and then it teaches, "whether he pinches [a bird-offering] or he sprinkles [its blood]."

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:3:1.hebrew: אלא הא והא - תרוייהו הנך מתניתא רבי שמעון דמתני', דפטר אשאר קרבנות בארבעה עשר ומחייב עלייהו במועד:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:3:1.english: Rather, [both] this and that - Both of those baraitot [follow] Rabbi Shimon of our Mishnah, who exempts [one] regarding other sacrifices on the fourteenth [of Nisan] and holds [one] liable for them on the festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:3:2.hebrew: מליקה אמליקה לא קשיא - קמייתא דפטר בארבעה עשר קאי, כדתני בה בהדיא. ותנא עוף, והוא הדין לשאר זבחים, אלא משום דאורחיה לעכוביה בו ביום אחר התמיד נקט ליה. ורישא דמתניתא בתרייתא, דקתני נמי "לא אמרו אלא פסח בלבד", רבי שמעון אמרה ואארבעה עשר קאי. ו"אחד השוחט כו'" דסיפא בחולו של מועד קאמר, ואשמעינן חיובא לזורק ולמולק כשוחט, דלא תימא שחיטה דווקא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:3:2.english: There is no contradiction between pinching and pinching - The first [baraita], which exempts [one who pinches], refers to the fourteenth [of Nisan], as it explicitly teaches in it. And it taught [the case of] a bird, though the same law applies to other sacrifices; rather, because it is usual to delay it on that day until after the daily offering, it mentioned it. And the first clause of the latter baraita, which also teaches, "They stated [this] only [regarding] the Passover offering alone," Rabbi Shimon said it, and it refers to the fourteenth [of Nisan]. And "Whether one slaughters, etc." of the latter clause speaks of the intermediate days of the festival, and it teaches us liability for one who throws [the blood] and for one who pinches [a bird] just like one who slaughters, so that you should not say [that liability applies] specifically to slaughtering.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:4:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - הני תרתי סתמי תנאי היא, ואליבא דרבי שמעון. מר מקיש הקטרה לעבודת הדם, הואיל וישנו בהלנת אימורין; ומר לית ליה האי היקישא, דשחיטה קאמר רחמנא, וזריקה דמתרביא בהדיא מדם זבחי, אבל הקטרה לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:4:1.english: It is [a dispute of] Tannaim - These two anonymous [baraitot] are [a dispute of] Tannaim, according to Rabbi Shimon. One master compares burning [the sacrificial parts] to the blood service, since it is subject to [the prohibition of] leaving the sacrificial parts overnight; and [the other] master does not hold of this comparison, for the Merciful One stated slaughtering, and sprinkling is explicitly included from "the blood of My sacrifice," but burning [is] not.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:6:1.hebrew: זבחי זבחי תרי זימני - תרי קראי כתיבי, שקיל י' דחד מינייהו ושדי אאידך, וקרי ביה זבח — דהיינו פסח — וקרי ביה זבחיי לשאר זבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:6:1.english: My sacrifice, My sacrifice, two times - Two verses are written; take the yod of one of them and cast [it] onto the other, and read it zevaḥ [sacrifice] — which is the Paschal offering — and read it zevaḥai [My sacrifices], [referring] to the rest of the offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:7:1.hebrew: ואמאי פלגינהו רחמנא - ולא כתב זבחיי בחד קרא, והכל במשמע, בין בפסח בין בשאר זבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:7:1.english: And why did the Merciful One divide them - and not write "My sacrifices" in one verse, [so that] everything [would be] included, whether the Paschal lamb [or] other sacrifices.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:7:2.hebrew: לומר לך בזמן דאיכא זבח - דהיינו פסח בארבעה עשר, לא מחייב אשאר זבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:7:2.english: To tell you: at the time when there is a sacrifice - that is, the Paschal [offering] on the fourteenth [of Nisan], one is not liable for other sacrifices.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:8:1.hebrew: הא סתמא פטור - מ"לא תשחט", דאמרינן כל כמה דלא עקר שם פסח מיניה, הוא פסח, ושחטו בשאר ימות השנה ופסול, ושחיטה שאינה ראויה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:8:1.english: But [when slaughtered] without [specific] intent, he is exempt - From [the prohibition of] "You shall not slaughter" [with leaven], for we say [that] as long as he has not uprooted the designation of a Paschal offering from it, it is a Paschal offering, and he slaughtered it during the rest of the days of the year and it is invalid, and it is an unfit slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 64a:9:1.hebrew: בעי עקירה - ולא אמרינן סתמיה שלמים הוא. ולשון בעיא הוא, כלומר: פשטינן לה מהכא או לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 64a:9:1.english: Requires uprooting - And we do not say that by default it is a peace-offering. And it is the language of an inquiry, that is to say: do we resolve it from here or not?

Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:14:1.hebrew: קראו את ההלל - פי': לוים, דתניא בתוספתא: "ישראל שוחטין את פסחיהן ולוים קוראים את ההלל". קשה לר"י, דאמרינן בפ' אין נערכין בערכין (יא.) ובכיצד מברכין (ברכות לה. ושם): "אין אומרים שירה אלא על היין", והכא חזינן דאיכא שירה בלא נסכים, וכן היו מקדשין העזרות בב' תודות ובשיר! ואומר ר"י דה"פ: אין אומרים שירה בשעת הקרבת קרבן אלא על היין, ד"משמח אלהים ואנשים" דריש ליה, ועיקר שתיה ושמחה היינו בשעת אכילה; ודומיא דהכי נמי לגבוה, בשעת הקרבת קרבן קאמר דאין אומר שירה אלא על היין, אבל שלא בשעת הקרבה היו אומרים שירה שלא על היין בכמה דוכתי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:14:1.english: They recited the Hallel - Explanation: [It was] the Levites [who recited it], as it is taught in the Tosefta: "Israelites slaughter their Paschal offerings, and the Levites recite the Hallel." This is difficult for the Ri, for we say in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ne'erakhin in Arakhin (11a) and in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 35a and there): "They do not recite song [in the Temple] except over wine," whereas here we see that there is song without libations, and similarly, they would sanctify the Temple courtyards with two thanks-offerings and with song! And the Ri says that this is its meaning: They do not recite song at the time of offering a sacrifice except over wine — for [the Gemara] expounds it from "[wine] that gladdens God and men," and the primary drinking and gladness is at the time of eating; and similarly for the Most High, it is at the time of offering a sacrifice that it says they do not recite song except over wine. However, not at the time of offering [a sacrifice], they would recite song without wine in several places.

Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:3:1.hebrew: הא והא רבי שמעון - נראה לר"י דההיא קמייתא לא הוה מצי לאוקומי כרבנן, משום דקתני בה: "אבל המולק את העוף בי"ד אינו עובר בולא כלום" — אמאי נקט עוף, אי לאו דאתא למידק דווקא בי"ד, אבל בחול המועד אפילו בעוף נמי מיחייב? והיינו כר' שמעון. ובקונטרס פי' לעיל טעם אחר אמאי נקט עוף:
Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:3:1.english: Both this [baraita] and that [baraita] are [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon - It appears to the Ri that [the Gemara] could not have established that first [baraita] in accordance with the Rabbis, because it teaches in it: "But one who pinches [the neck of] a bird on the fourteenth [of Nisan] does not transgress anything at all" — why did it specify a bird, if not that it comes to imply [that this applies] specifically on the fourteenth, whereas on Chol HaMoed one is liable even for a bird? And this is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. And in the Kuntres [Rashi], he explained earlier another reason why it specified a bird:

Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:4:1.hebrew: ואיכא דלא מקיש - חלב לזבח. ונהי דלא מקיש להקטרה, לענין הכי מקיש, דלא אמרינן אפילו אחד בסוף העולם, דסברא הוא לאקושי להכי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:4:1.english: And there is one who does not compare - [the] fat to [the] sacrifice. And although he does not compare [them] with respect to burning, with respect to this [matter] he does compare [them], so that we do not say [that one is liable] even [if] someone at the end of the world [possesses leaven], because it is logical to compare [them] for this [purpose].

Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:8:1.hebrew: טעמא שלא לשמו הא סתמא פטור ש"מ כו' - זאת גירסת רש"י, ואין נראה לר"ת, דהא איכא למידק מרישא איפכא. וגריס ר"ת הכי: "לשמו אמאי פטור? שלמים לשם פסח קשחיט; ש"מ בעי עקירה". פירוש: דאי לא בעי עקירה, אפילו שחט לשמו כשר, דשלמים לשם פסח כשר, דהא מכשיר לעיל ר' יהושע שוחט אחרים לשמו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 64a:8:1.english: "The reason [is that he slaughtered it] for a different purpose; had [he slaughtered it] without specific intent, he would be exempt. Learn from this, etc." - This is Rashi's textual reading, but it does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for one can infer the opposite from the first clause [of the Mishnah]. And Rabbeinu Tam reads [the text] as follows: "For its own purpose, why is he exempt? He is slaughtering peace-offerings for the sake of a Paschal lamb! Learn from this [that] it requires uprooting [of its designation]." Explanation: For if it did not require uprooting, even if he slaughtered it for its own purpose it would be valid, since peace-offerings [slaughtered] for the sake of a Paschal lamb are valid, as Rabbi Yehoshua rules valid above one who slaughters other [offerings] for its purpose.
